Alright well, first welcome to Android.

I would recommend rooting your device first off (before you get too attached to anything) as unlocking/rooting may very well 'factory reset' your device. If you're even a little inclined to do it at some point, do it now. It'll make things easier for the long run.

Just google 'root <mydevicename>' and you should find plenty of details (some may require a PC connection and/or installing software on your PC).

Alright now that you've gotten root I recommend, TitaniumBackup

It's a great backup application and it also can 'decrapify' your phone if there are apps that you don't want but can't uninstall (looking at YOU HP Print Services). Note You may be unable to get OTA(over the air) updates if you remove these applications so possibly beware there. Honestly the backup feature is stellar.

Next up is (if you're on stock/don't want a custom ROM) is to install GravityBox (which requires you to also install Xposed Framework). Secondarily XDA is a great resource for your device, it will have custom ROM's Kernels and a ton of other stuff if you poke around there under your device's sub forum. GravityBox just exposes a ton of tweaks that are usually only available by flashing a custom ROM.

Alright now some apps:

  • Firefox or Dolphin Browser

  • FDroid use this to install AdAway

  • ESFile Explorer - to browse your folders/directories

That should do it to get you started. Another path that you may want to venture down is to check out alternative OS's (like CyanogenMod) .

Aptoide and F-Droid. These are especially useful if you don't have a Google account.
